scope.summary: Deliver the first operator-usable Ferric Forager production slice: the shipped fforager entrypoint accepts one representative direct HTTP/HTTPS media input, resolves and selects it through the production engine, acquires bytes through the approved production transport, commits a validated durable output and archive result, emits structured diagnostics, and runs with an independent failure-isolated watcher.
in_scope: Create only the accepted Section 9 product packages and private modules required by this direct-HTTP vertical slice; no skeleton-only package may close the packet.

Expose the shipped fforager command through the launcher/CLI composition path; the launcher owns a separately terminable worker and independent watcher as siblings, and the worker executes the one engine path rather than duplicating behavior in frontends.
Accept one committed deterministic direct HTTP/HTTPS media fixture through a supervised local protocol-server boundary and produce a validated operator-visible output.
Resolve the input into the canonical serializable source graph, apply deterministic representation selection, and preserve stable job, source, asset, output, archive, and diagnostic identities.

Use the approved FF-DEC-002 ordinary transport boundary with Ferric-owned address admission, redirect, cookie, proxy, retry, timeout, cancellation, backpressure, and receipt policy; fingerprint-required cases remain typed unsupported and never fall back to wreq.

Exercise real job lifecycle, atomic resource admission, byte bounds, cancellation, typed events/errors, staged output, journal durability, resume validation, startup reconciliation, archive insertion, cleanup, and success only after output/archive agreement.

Start the minimum independent watcher as a sibling process through governed startup, prove bounded Ready/degraded behavior, preserve crash evidence, and prove watcher absence, crash, incompatibility, hang, or storage failure cannot change Ferric correctness or the decided result.

Build the locked release profile once, record the artifact digest, stage that exact product artifact outside source/build/governance roots, and execute success, negative, cancellation, recovery, watcher-degraded, and required-observable counterfactual scenarios through the shipped entrypoint.

Extend executable packet-promotion validation to parse exact dependency IDs and require each named predecessor to be VALIDATED with its closure commit contained in canonical main; missing, ranged, alternative, superseded, uncontained, or self-asserted bindings fail closed so WP-FF-011 cannot activate early.
Update product/MODEL_MANUAL.md with exact commands, inputs, outputs, navigation, diagnostics, safety limits, failures, and recovery for behavior that actually passes runtime proof.
non_goals: HLS, DASH, MSS, FFmpeg processing, JavaScript challenges, generic extraction, collections, live recording, broad post-processing, or full yt-dlp replacement parity.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: The exact staged release fforager launcher, worker, and watcher artifacts accept the committed representative direct HTTP/HTTPS fixture through the production entrypoint, launcher-owned sibling topology, worker engine, approved production transport, source graph, selection, storage, diagnostics, and operator-visible result; the launcher exits zero only after producing the expected hash-bound durable output and reconciled archive result within the declared timeout.

Production-runtime cancellation and transport-failure scenarios exercise the shipped artifact and prove bounded cancellation progress, complete resource release, no corrupt final output, typed nonzero failure, retained diagnostics, and no success or archive insertion before required effects are acknowledged.

Crash/restart runtime scenarios cover every implemented durable prefix, run reconciliation twice, reject inconsistent resume state, and produce the same correct output/archive verdict without advancing beyond durable bytes or deleting recoverable evidence early.

The staged launcher starts an independent watcher with bounded readiness and shutdown; missing, corrupt, incompatible, hung, crashed, and storage-failed watcher scenarios expose diagnostics degradation while leaving the same Ferric bytes, archive decision, exit semantics, and bounded launcher completion, and an uncommanded Ferric crash leaves retrievable watcher evidence.

The product dependency and execution graph contains no Python, yt-dlp, yt-dlp companion asset, wreq product route, testkit normal/build edge, hidden governance/build runtime read, unapproved process, or undeclared native/runtime dependency; an indirect-wrapper negative fixture fails the canonical gate.

A backwards-compatible FF-GATE-RUNTIME-001 proof-contract extension builds once; hashes and stages every exact release artifact; supervises the deterministic HTTP origin, launcher, product process, and independent watcher; executes ordered success, transport-failure, external-cancellation, crash/restart/reconciliation, and watcher-degraded actions with real production adapters; semantically inspects output, archive, journal, and watcher evidence; and rejects a declaration-preserving mutation of product behavior or durable state. Prior ff.runtime-proof@1 fixtures continue to pass, and an independent validator that did not author the proof producer reruns the gate.

The no-context model manual names only runtime-proven commands and accurately documents purpose, startup, inputs, outputs, navigation, stable diagnostics, limits, common failures, recovery, watcher degradation, and artifact-proof reproduction; executing its canonical workflow reproduces the accepted result.

FF-GATE-ARCH-001, FF-GATE-PR-001, FF-GATE-RUNTIME-001, triggered deep/fault/platform gates, FF-GATE-WATCHER-001, secret scan, artifact hygiene, and independent HIGH-risk adversarial review pass for one source, lockfile, fixture, artifact, watcher, and runtime-proof manifest with no unresolved finding.
